chunks: From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Mu'ammar al-Zayyat, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man comes to me and says, 'Lend me dinars so that I may buy oil with them and then sell it to you.' He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to borrow money to buy goods and sell them back to the lender?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies the permissibility of a specific trade arrangement where a borrower purchases goods (oil) to sell back to the lender, confirming Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) approval with 'la ba'sa'. It highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding commercial transactions, distinguishing this practice from riba (usury) by focusing on the actual exchange of goods rather than a simple loan-for-money swap. The hadith underscores the importance of intent and the structure of the transaction in validating trade within the Islamic economic framework.
